newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed Friday as traders digested Thursday's dramatic rally, as well as monthly inventory data released late Thursday showing an increase in U.S. consumer coffee stocks.

"The market could probably come in 5.00 (cents a lb) higher or 5.00 cents lower," one trader said. "We're going with unchanged because no one knows what's going to happen and we're not sure how it's going to react to the stocks."
Supplies of green coffee housed in U.S. warehouses rose in April by 198,000 60-kg bags, to 1,855,000 bags, the Green Coffee Association of New York reported.
Most analysts said the figures were mainly neutral and in with market expectations of a build up of between 100,000 and 300,000 bags.
Thursday, New York arabica futures surged, with spot May exploding to levels not seen since in 20 years, as speculators led a broad-based buying frenzy amid a background of tight supply.
The board set new life-of-contract highs, with benchmark July soaring more that 20 cents per lb at one point to a peak of 262.00 cents, before a round of profit-taking pared gains.

July settled at 255.20 cents a lb, up 14.60 cents -- or six percent -- on the day. Spot May ended up 15.55 cents at 277.05 cents after peaking at 279.00 cents, its highest price since 1977. The back months closed 6.00 to 11.65 higher.
Technically, traders pegged July support at 248 to 246, while resistance was seen at yesterday's high of 279.

After the close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks continued to climb. Stocks increased by 1,770 bags, to 37,182 bags as of May 12. There were 18,040 bags of coffee pending grading, the exchange said.
London robusta futures jumped to 15-1/2 month highs early Friday, but by midday some of the gains were pared. LIFFE July was up $101 at the break, to $2,034, after peaking at $2,060.
